title: Go: Testing with go test
description: Write unit tests in Go using the testing package — basic tests, table-driven patterns, helpers, and subtests.

steps.title: Basic Test function
steps.description: Write a function `Add(a, b int) int` that returns a+b. Create a test `TestAdd` that calls `Add(2, 3)` and checks the result equals 5 using `t.Errorf` if wrong. Print "TestAdd passed" on success.

verification.failureMessage: Make sure the test function has the correct signature.

steps.title: t.Errorf vs t.Fatal
steps.description: Create a function `Divide(a, b float64) float64`. Test that `Divide(10, 0)` prints an error. Demonstrate the difference: `Errorf` logs and continues, `Fatalf` stops the test immediately.
hints: `t.Errorf` reports failure but continues the test
`t.Fatalf` reports failure and stops the current test immediately
Both take format strings like fmt.Printf

verification.successMessage: You understand Errorf vs Fatalf behavior!
verification.failureMessage: Write two test cases demonstrating both functions.

steps.title: Table-driven tests
steps.description: Write a function `IsEven(n int) bool`. Test it with a table of cases: `{name, input, expected}`. Loop over the table and run each case, printing "Test: <name> — got <result>".
hints: Define a slice of anonymous structs for your test cases

verification.failureMessage: Define test cases as a slice of structs with name, input, expected.

steps.title: Helper functions (t.Helper)
steps.description: Create a helper function `assertEqual(t testing.TB, got, want any)` that calls `t.Helper()` so failures point to the caller. Write a test using this helper and make it fail to show the correct line.
hints: Call `t.Helper()` at the start of the helper function
Use `testing.TB` interface to accept both *testing.T and *testing.B
Without t.Helper(), failure line numbers point inside the helper

verification.successMessage: Helpers with t.Helper() give correct line numbers!
verification.failureMessage: Make sure t.Helper() is called before any other code in the helper.

steps.title: Subtests with t.Run
steps.description: Test a `Max(a, b int) int` function using `t.Run` for subtest names "positive", "negative", "zero". Each subtest exercises a different scenario. Print "All sub-tests done".
hints: Subtests can be run selectively with `go test -run TestMax/positive`
Each subtest is independent — one failing doesn't affect others

verification.failureMessage: Use t.Run to create named subtests for each scenario.
